proposals.before: Right Canal, peril and extinction followed in turn—Heaven's mandate may be feared, mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.
proposals.after: Youqu met ruin in turn; Heaven's mandate is to be feared, and mountains and rivers cannot be relied upon.
proposals.reason: 右渠 is the personal name Youqu, king of Gojoseon, not the common-noun phrase ‘Right Canal’; paired with 餘善 at the end of s0189, the sentence says the two rulers met ruin in turn.

proposals.before: Right Canal, [12] peril and extinction followed in turn—Heaven's mandate may be feared, mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.
proposals.after: Youqu met ruin in turn; Heaven's mandate is to be feared, and mountains and rivers cannot be relied upon.
proposals.reason: The English must preserve 右渠 as King Youqu's name and omit the editorial footnote marker; the sentence invokes Yu Shan and Youqu as rulers whose defensible terrain did not save them.

decisions.reason: In this sequence of historical exemplars, 右渠 is King Youqu of Gojoseon. The preceding unit ends with 餘善, so the two units together state that Yu Shan and Youqu met ruin in turn; a literal reading as ‘Right Canal’ is impossible here.
The idiomatic revision correctly treats Youqu as a personal name, joins naturally to Yu Shan in the preceding unit, and removes the editorial note marker from the prose.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 餘善、（石）右渠，危亡繼及，天命可畏，山川難恃
